entities.summary: Yin Wenzi, a foundational text of the School of Names, was penned by the Chinese philosopher and logician Yin Wen (349–283 BCE) during the Warring States period. Born in the state of Qi, Yin Wen was a key figure in the intellectual debates of the time, often collaborating with other prominent thinkers like Gongsun Long. His philosophical ideas, as outlined in the Yin Wenzi, would significantly influence the development of Daoist and Confucian thought. Yin Wen's significance lies in his contributions to the fields of logic, epistemology, and the classification of concepts, which continue to shape philosophical discourse to this day. As a testament to his enduring impact, the Yin Wenzi has been translated into numerous languages and remains a cornerstone of Chinese philosophical heritage.
